top_backlinks.title: Candor Medical | Alternative Telehealth Consultations Australia

notes.verdict_label: Don't fight the brand. Take the category.
notes.tagline: A near-pure brand fortress. 12.7K visits / mo and 96% of it is the word 'candor'. Outside the brand, almost nothing — 10 treatments pages, 8 education posts, almost zero organic non-brand. They bought the brand with paid; organic is the rounding error.

visual_system: Minimal, modern medical aesthetic — sage, cream, generous whitespace.
Stock-feeling imagery — fewer real patient or clinician portraits than Polln or Alternaleaf.
Calm typography, soft rounded UI, conservative colour use.
App / portal lives on a dedicated subdomain (app.candormedical.com).
site_architecture: /treatments — 10 condition / category pages (alternative therapy, hair loss, ED, contraceptive pill, herpes, weight loss).
No locations, no city pages, no practitioner roster, no library at scale.
tone_compliance: Conservative copy — telehealth-first framing, light on specific claims.
Treatments pages are short and templated, not evidence-led.
No bylined authors or medical-reviewer disclosure on education posts.
Brand-led — copy assumes the user already knows Candor.

eeat.notes: Technical baseline is clean (HTTPS, CWV, app subdomain). YMYL signals are weak — no authorship on education posts, no medical-reviewer block, thin schema, low freshness. The site behaves like a brand landing surface, not an organic content engine.

steal.note: Their /treatments/{condition} URL pattern is sound — replicate the structure but author the content properly with citations and clinician sign-off.
Patient portal on app. earns clean brand+nav traffic and keeps the marketing site light. Standard pattern — adopt.
Speed, schema-light, no bloat. Whatever stack we ship, keep it lean.

avoid.evidence: 96% of organic traffic is the literal word 'candor' and misspellings. Outside the brand, the organic engine is ~561 visits / mo. If brand demand stalls, the site stalls.
10 /treatments pages ranking, 9 of them earn 0–1 visits / mo. Published but not winning — thin content, no E-E-A-T.
8 /education posts → ~6 visits / mo total. Anonymous authorship, no medical reviewer, no freshness — invisible on YMYL search.
No /locations, no city pages, no 'near me' coverage. Brand-fortress strategies don't scale into local intent.

implications: Candor proves the brand-paid playbook works — but doesn't translate to organic moat.
The category is wide open against them — almost every non-brand query is undefended.
Their /treatments URL pattern is the only thing worth copying structurally; the content is empty.
Hellomello wins by being the category-first site they aren't — locations, conditions, library, named practitioners.

gap_matrix.comment: Don't fight here. They've already bought it.
Brand search includes 'candor medical reviews' — defensive gap for them, attack for us.
app. subdomain earns 761 visits — they have it right.
Single /faq page. Long-tail informational is empty.
